newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends weaker in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends weaker in moderate trade.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended weaker on Thursday at C$1.3650 (US$0.7326) from this morning's open of C$1.3615 (US$0.7344) in moderate afternoon trading, dealer said. * They said the currency strengthened from the open to about C$1.3600 (US$0.7352) by mid-morning before stop-loss selling emerged to drive the unit weaker in the afternoon.
Canada's dollar ended weaker on Thursday at C$1.3650 (US$0.7326) from this morning's open of C$1.3615 (US$0.7344) in moderate afternoon trading.
Dealers said the currency strengthened from the open to about C$1.3600 (US$0.7352) by mid-morning before stop-loss selling emerged to take it weaker in the afternoon.
They said trading in the currency was so mixed throughout the day that it was tough to decide which way the unit would trade overnight.
"The buying of Canada this morning was very substantial but similarly we are closing up on a weak note," one said.
Traders said widespread buying interest in the U.S. dollar, which included trade against the Canadian dollar, also added to the Canadian currency's weakness.

They said investors bought U.S. dollars in expectation of higher U.S. interest rates and on a news report that a senior German central bank official did not object to recent dollar gains versus the mark.

Speculation has risen in the markets that the Federal Reserve might hike U.S. interest rates since its chairman Alan Greenspan said earlier this month that the U.S. central bank could push up rates to pre-empt the growth of inflation.

The U.S dollar rose to 1.7065 marks from Wednesday's close of 1.6925 marks and rose to 123.40 yen from 122.15 yen. Canada's dollar remained strong on the crosses, rising to 1.2490 marks from Wednesday's 1.2414 and jumped to 90.30 yen from 89.62 yen.
